Privacy information

Last updated 8 November 2026

This page explains what happens to your data when you use the page guide, the AI avatar on this site. The welcome and prewritten portfolio answers run locally in your browser. Typed questions use those prewritten answers until you start a live guide session. It does not ask for your name or sign you up for anything.

What the guide is

The guide is an AI avatar with a look-alike face and a synthetic voice. It is not a live person. It answers questions about my professional experience and public projects, and its answers can be wrong. Please do not share private information with it.

It is off until you turn it on

Opening the portfolio downloads fonts from Google Fonts and the Cloudflare Web Analytics script. Choosing Start avatar or Use voice also downloads the guide’s JavaScript from avatar.pixeltronic.dev. These resource requests occur before you start the guide and expose ordinary connection information, such as your network address, to the servers serving them.

Downloading those resources does not start a conversation or request microphone access. Turning on the guide opens a dialog. A conversation session is requested only after you enter a pass key, agree to the notice, and press Start. Voice recording requires a separate tap on the microphone.

What happens when you start a conversation

  • Your pass key is sent to my server, which checks it. The server keeps only a one-way hash of each key, together with its label, expiry date, and how many sessions and seconds it has used.
  • Typed questions go to my server and from there to Anthropic, whose Claude model writes the reply. The server keeps the last few messages in memory for the length of the session only.
  • Reply text goes to ElevenLabs, which turns it into speech.
  • Reply audio goes to Simli, which renders the avatar video. The video stream runs between your browser and Simli.
  • Voice questions are recorded in your browser for up to 30 seconds, only after you tap the microphone, and sent to my server. They are transcribed there by a speech model running on the server itself, so the recording is not passed to a third party. It is processed in memory and not saved. The text you see after "You said:" is then handled like a typed question.

Each of these providers handles data under its own terms and may process it outside your country. I do not control their retention. A session lasts at most five minutes.

What I keep

  • Conversations are not stored. Once a session ends, the questions and replies are gone from my server. Your transcript stays visible in your own browser tab until you leave or reload the page.
  • Pass key records (hash, label, expiry, usage) are kept for as long as the key is valid.
  • Failed-key counters. To stop guessing, the server briefly remembers your network address after repeated wrong keys. It is removed once the lock window has passed.
  • No request logging. Request bodies and query strings are not logged, and the web proxy's access log is switched off.
  • Backups of the database (keys, usage, access requests) are kept for 14 days.

Requesting access

If you use the request form, I store your name, the contact you give, and your optional message so that I can reply. A scrambled form of your network address is stored with it to limit repeated requests. I use this only to answer your request, and I delete it afterwards.

In your browser

If you tick "Remember on this device", your pass key is saved in your browser's local storage so you do not have to type it again. Otherwise it is held only for the current tab. "Forget key" removes it. The guide itself sets no cookies.

Site statistics

The portfolio page uses Cloudflare Web Analytics to count visits in aggregate. The guide itself adds no tracking.

Your rights

You can ask what I hold about you, ask me to correct or delete it, or object to its use. Use the request form and say that it is a privacy request. If you are in the EU, you can also complain to your local data protection authority.
